STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r7.claim: The opposition of affluent and powerful people to prophets recurs throughout this surah, as elsewhere in the Quran.
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r7.anchor: The opposition to prophets by the affluent and powerful is a recurrent theme in this sūrah

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p173/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p173/r1.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p173/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir, Nafi, Abu Amr, and Asim read خرجا without alif here and in the first occurrence in al-Muminun, but خراج with alif in its final occurrence.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p173/r1.anchor: فقرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وعاصم: خرجا، وفي المؤمنين: خرجا بغير ألف. فخراج الأخير بألف.

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p173/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p173/r2.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p173/r2.claim: Ibn Amir omits alif in all three forms; Hamza and al-Kisai include alif in all three.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p173/r2.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر: خرجا بغير ألف، وفي المؤمنين خرجا بغير ألف، (فخرج ربك) بغير ألف في الثلاثة.

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p173/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p173/r3.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p173/r3.claim: خرج is a gift paid from their wealth, while خراج usually denotes a land levy; al-Ajaj attests broader use of خراج.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p173/r3.anchor: قال أبو علي: هل نجعل لك خرجا: أي: هل نجعل لك عطية نخرجها إليك من أموالنا،

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p173/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p173/r4.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p173/r4.claim: The offered payment is a gift rather than a land tax, as indicated by the offer and Dhu al-Qarnayn's answer that his Lord's provision is better.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p173/r4.anchor: ويدل على أن الخراج العطية منهم له، قوله في جوابه لهم: ما مكني فيه ربي خير

IBNMUJAHID:v1p400/r1.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p400/r1.speaker: author
IBNMUJAHID:v1p400/r1.claim: Ibn Kathīr, Nāfiʿ, ʿĀṣim, and Abū ʿAmr omit alif in kharjan here and at 23:72 but retain it in fa-kharāju rabbik; Ibn ʿĀmir omits it in all three; Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī use it throughout.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p400/r1.anchor: 37 واختلفوا فى قوله ﴿ فهل نجعل لك خرجا ﴾ 94 وقوله فى المؤمنين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p574/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p574/r10.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p574/r10.claim: The question about payment rebukes the audience: perhaps they reject the Prophet because they think he is asking them for money.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p574/r10.anchor: أم تسألهم خرجا هذا استفهام توبيخ أيضا المعنى بل أتسألهم مالا فغلبوا لذلك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p574/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p574/r11.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p574/r11.claim: Al-Zamakhshari argues that even a small fee from people would be inferior to the greater reward from the Creator.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p574/r11.anchor: أم تسألهم على هدايتك لهم قليلا من عطاء الخلق والكثير من عطاء الخالق خير

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p574/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p574/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p574/r12.claim: The passage removes their excuses: the Messenger is known among them, seeks no worldly wealth, calls only to Islam, exposes their blind following and lack of reflection, and has clear signs.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p574/r12.anchor: فقد ألزمهم الحجة في هذه الآيات، وقطع معاذيرهم وعللهم بأن الذي أرسل إليهم رجل معروف أمره وحاله

ZAJJAJ:v4p19/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p19/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p19/r5.claim: The question means: do you ask them for payment for what you have brought them?
ZAJJAJ:v4p19/r5.anchor: أي (أم تسألهم) على ما أتيتهم به أجرا.

ZAJJAJ:v4p19/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p19/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p19/r6.claim: A reading is reported with خراجا for the first word, matching خراج in the second phrase.

ASAD-NOTES:23:72/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:23:72/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:23:72/r1.claim: The Prophet seeks no worldly payment from them; God's recompense is better because He is the best provider.
ASAD-NOTES:23:72/r1.anchor: Or dost thou [O Muhammad] ask of them any worldly recompense? But [they ought to know that]

ASAD-NOTES:23:72#n44/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:23:72#n44/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:23:72#n44/r1.claim: Kharj and kharaj are broadly synonymous, both meaning recompense.
ASAD-NOTES:23:72#n44/r1.anchor: The terms kharj and kharaj which occur in the above verse are more or less synonymous, both of them denoting "recompense".

ASAD-NOTES:23:72#n44/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:23:72#n44/r2.speaker: Zamakhshari
ASAD-NOTES:23:72#n44/r2.claim: Zamakhshari sees kharj as slightly narrower than kharaj; Asad's translation marks the first as worldly recompense and leaves God's recompense unrestricted to this world or the hereafter.
ASAD-NOTES:23:72#n44/r2.anchor: According to Zamakhshari, however, there is a slight difference between these two expressions, kharj being more restricted in its meaning than kharaj

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p269/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p269/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p269/r2.claim: The passage rebukes the disbelievers’ carelessness, then reassures the Prophet not to lose hope: he is on the right path, they have strayed, and they will see their fate.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p269/r2.anchor: he should not lose hope because of their stubbornness and arrogance; he is on the right path and these people have deviated from it

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p269/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p269/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p269/r6.claim: The concluding challenge exposes their contradiction: they acknowledge and affirm truth, then state its opposite and go astray.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p269/r6.anchor: on the one hand, they accept and declare the truth, but then they lose their senses and state what is the opposite

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p273/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p273/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p273/r5.claim: The Prophet gives freely what he received freely and asks no fee; opponents who disregard the favor deprive themselves, and rejection cannot harm him.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p273/r5.anchor: he is distributing free what he gained free and not asking them for any charges.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p273/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p273/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p273/r6.claim: God's reward is superior, and He provides for His messengers' truth-preaching; righteous people who continue their work likewise receive its provisions.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p273/r6.anchor: God’s messengers are advocates of the truth; their preaching has all its provisions.

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p298#2/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p298#2/r1.speaker: ابن عامر
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p298#2/r1.claim: Ibn Amir reads kharjan without alif in both occurrences.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p298#2/r1.anchor: قرأ ابن عامر (خرجا فخرج ربك) [المؤمنون/ 72] بغير ألف

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p298#2/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p298#2/r2.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وعاصم
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p298#2/r2.claim: Ibn Kathir, Nafi, Abu Amr, and Asim read the first word without alif and the second with alif.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p298#2/r2.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وعاصم: خرجا بغير ألف فخراج ربك بألف

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p298#2/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p298#2/r3.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p298#2/r3.claim: Hamza and al-Kisai read both forms with alif.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p298#2/r3.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي (خراجا، فخراج ربك) في الحرفين جميعا بألف

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p298#2/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p298#2/r4.speaker: أبو عبيدة
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p298#2/r4.claim: Abu Ubayda says a servant pays a kharj as his yield or rent, and subjects pay kharj to a ruler; the word can also denote rain from a cloud, as al-Hudhalī explains its name.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p298#2/r4.anchor: أبو عبيدة: العبد يؤدي إليك خرجه، أي: غلته، والرعية تؤدي إلى الأمير الخرج

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p298#2/r5.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p298#2/r5.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p298#2/r5.claim: Kharj can mean whatever is paid out to its recipient, even when it is not a tax; al-Ajjaj's يوم خراج supports this broader sense, while kharāj is the specific land tax.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p298#2/r5.anchor: الخرج: ما يخرج إلى من يخرج ذلك إليه وإن لم يكن ذلك ضريبة

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p298#2/r6.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p298#2/r6.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p298#2/r6.claim: Kharāj is the proper name for the land levy, as the cited poem about the land tax illustrates; kharj can nonetheless be used more generally.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p298#2/r6.anchor: والاسم الأخص بالضريبة المضروبة على الأرضين الخراج

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p298#2/r7.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p298#2/r7.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p298#2/r7.claim: On Ibn Kathir and the others' mixed reading, the question means they are asked for no payment; God's kharāj is better because He imposed the land dues and capitation, as elsewhere the Prophet says he asks no wage.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p298#2/r7.anchor: فمعنى هذا: بأموال الخراج، وإذا كان كذلك فقول ابن كثير ومن تبعه: خرجا فخراج ربك خير معناه

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p298#2/r8.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p298#2/r8.speaker: أبو الحسن
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p298#2/r8.claim: Abu al-Hasan says he cannot determine which of kharj and kharāj is more common in Arabic speech.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p298#2/r8.anchor: قال أبو الحسن: لا أدري أيهما أكثر في كلام العرب

NASHR:v2p329/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p329/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p329/r1.claim: The author points back to earlier discussions of the variant readings in خرجا and فخراج ربك, without restating the forms here.
NASHR:v2p329/r1.anchor: وتقدم اختلافهم في خرجا، وفي فخراج ربك في الكهف

QIRAAT-ER:23:72:3#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:23:72:3#1/r1.speaker: Lvw
QIRAAT-ER:23:72:3#1/r1.claim: The standard kharj then kharāj forms contrast a specific payment with systematic revenue.
QIRAAT-ER:23:72:3#1/r1.anchor: Lvw, mutawatir: Standard reading: kharj (faʿl) in first position, kharāj (faʿāl) in second — morphological contrast

QIRAAT-ER:23:72:3#2/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:23:72:3#2/r1.speaker: Lvw
QIRAAT-ER:23:72:3#2/r1.claim: The variant uses kharj in both positions, removing the distinction between a specific payment and systematic revenue.
QIRAAT-ER:23:72:3#2/r1.anchor: Lvw, mutawatir: "Canonical variant: both positions use kharj (faʿl) — eliminates morphological contrast

QIRAAT-ER:23:72:3#3/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:23:72:3#3/r1.speaker: Lvw
QIRAAT-ER:23:72:3#3/r1.claim: The variant uses kharāj in both positions, making the first term “revenue/tax” and suggesting systematic extraction in both domains.
QIRAAT-ER:23:72:3#3/r1.anchor: Lvw, mutawatir: "Canonical variant: both positions use kharāj (faʿāl) — elevates the first to ""revenue/tax

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p47#4/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p47#4/r3.speaker: الحسن
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p47#4/r3.claim: Al-Hasan glosses kharjan as payment or wages.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p47#4/r3.anchor: عن الحسن في قوله تعالى ﴿ تسألهم خرجا ﴾ قال أجرا

ALUSI-FULL:v18p53#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p53#3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p53#3/r1.claim: This links to the preceding أم يقولون به جنة (23:70) and shifts to another rebuke: do they allege that the Prophet seeks payment for delivering the message?
ALUSI-FULL:v18p53#3/r1.anchor: فهو انتقال إلى توبيخ آخر وغير للخطاب لمناسبته ما بعده وكان المراد أم يزعمون

ALUSI-FULL:v18p53#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p53#3/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p53#3/r2.claim: خرج means a payment or fee.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p53#3/r2.anchor: أي جعلا فلأجل ذلك لا يؤمنون بك

ALUSI-FULL:v18p53#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p53#3/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p53#3/r3.claim: The Lord's provision in this world and reward in the next are better than their fee because they are abundant, lasting, and free from human obligation; this explains the implied denial that the Prophet asks them.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p53#3/r3.anchor: أي رزقه في الدنيا وثوابه في الآخرة تعليل لنفي السؤال المستفاد من الإنكار

ALUSI-FULL:v18p53#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p53#3/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p53#3/r4.claim: Calling God the Prophet's Lord reinforces the argument and honors the Prophet.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p53#3/r4.anchor: وفي التعرض لعنوان الربوبية مع الإضافة إلى ضميره عليه الصلاة والسلام من تعليل الحكم وتشريفه

ALUSI-FULL:v18p53#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p53#3/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p53#3/r5.claim: خرج is anything given out, opposite دخل; خراج commonly means a land tax and suggests greater, recurring obligation. Some distinguish voluntary خرج from obligatory خراج; others say خرج is broader or treat them as synonyms.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p53#3/r5.anchor: يقال لكل ما تخرجه إلى غيرك والخراج غالب في الضريبة على الأرض ففيه إشعار بالكثرة واللزوم

ALUSI-FULL:v18p53#3/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p53#3/r6.speaker: ابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي والحسن وعيسى
ALUSI-FULL:v18p53#3/r6.claim: Ibn Amir reads خرجا فخرج; Hamza and al-Kisai read خراجا فخراج by lexical matching; al-Hasan and Isa read خراجا فخرج.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p53#3/r6.anchor: للمشاكلة وقرأ الحسن وعيسى ( خراجا فخرج ) وكأن اختيار

ALUSI-FULL:v18p53#3/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p53#3/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p53#3/r7.claim: Using خراج for the Prophet's side may emphasize their entrenched disbelief, while using خرج for God lowers their payment: even a little from God is better than much from them.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p53#3/r7.anchor: للإشارة إلى قوة تمكنهم في الكفر

ALUSI-FULL:v18p53#3/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p53#3/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p53#3/r8.claim: The final clause reinforces the superiority of God's provision: the best provider gives better than others.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p53#3/r8.anchor: تأكيد لخيرية خراجه سبحانه وتعالى فإن من كان خير الرازقين يكون رزقه خيرا من رزق غيره

ALUSI-FULL:v18p53#3/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p53#3/r9.speaker: الجبائي
ALUSI-FULL:v18p53#3/r9.claim: Al-Jubba'i infers that no one equals God in beneficence, while human beings can provide one another.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p53#3/r9.anchor: واستدل الجبائي بذلك على أنه سبحانه لا يساويه أحد في الأفضال على عباده

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p424#3/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p424#3/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p424#3/r4.claim: Kharj means a wage or payment for what the Prophet brought them.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p424#3/r4.anchor: {أم تسألهم} على ما جئتهم به، {خرجا} أجرا وجعلا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p424#3/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p424#3/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p424#3/r5.claim: What God gives of provision and reward is better, and He is the best provider.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p424#3/r5.anchor: أي: ما يعطيك الله من رزقه وثوابه خير، {وهو خير الرازقين}

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p424#3/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p424#3/r6.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وابن عامر
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p424#3/r6.claim: Hamza and al-Kisa'i read both forms with alif; Ibn Amir reads both without it; the other readers omit alif in the first form and retain it in the second.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p424#3/r6.anchor: قرأ حمزة والكسائي: "خراجا" "فخراج" كلاهما بالألف، وقرأ ابن عامر كلاهما بغير ألف

BAYDAWI-FULL:23:72-73/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:72-73/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:72-73/r1.claim: This alternative question corresponds to the earlier question whether he was possessed.

BAYDAWI-FULL:23:72-73/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:72-73/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:72-73/r2.claim: Kharj means payment for delivering the message.

BAYDAWI-FULL:23:72-73/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:72-73/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:72-73/r3.claim: God's kharāj is either sustenance in this life or reward in the afterlife.
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:72-73/r3.anchor: رزقه في الدنيا أو ثوابه في العقبى

BAYDAWI-FULL:23:72-73/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:72-73/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:72-73/r4.claim: God's provision is better for its breadth and permanence, leaving the Messenger no need to take their payment.
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:72-73/r4.anchor: لسعته ودوامه ففيه مندوحة لك عن عطائهم

BAYDAWI-FULL:23:72-73/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:72-73/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:72-73/r5.claim: Kharj is what one gives another; kharāj usually means land tax, suggesting abundant, continuing payment.
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:72-73/r5.anchor: والخرج بإزاء الدخل يقال لكل ما تخرجه إلى غيرك

BAYDAWI-FULL:23:72-73/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:72-73/r7.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:72-73/r7.claim: Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read khirājan fa-kharāj for matching sound-patterns.

BAYDAWI-FULL:23:72-73/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:72-73/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:72-73/r8.claim: The closing clause confirms the superiority of God's provision.

BAYDAWI-FULL:23:72-73/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:72-73/r10.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:72-73/r10.claim: The verses eliminate grounds for denial and accusation, leaving hatred of truth or lack of discernment.
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:72-73/r10.anchor: حصر أقسام ما يؤدي إلى الإنكار والاتهام

BIQAI-FULL:v5p212/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p212/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p212/r11.claim: After refuting their objections about the message and Messenger, the author points out that they know he asks no payment, removing another possible suspicion.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p212/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p212/r12.speaker: البغوي
BIQAI-FULL:v5p212/r12.claim: Al-Baghawi glosses kharj as payment or a reward.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p212/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p212/r13.speaker: ابن مكتوم
BIQAI-FULL:v5p212/r13.claim: Ibn Maktum says kharj and kharaj can be an annual, measured levy from communal wealth; kharaj can also mean a slave’s or bondwoman’s earnings.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p212/r13.anchor: الخرج والخراج شيء يخرجه القوم في السنة

BIQAI-FULL:v5p212/r14.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p212/r14.speaker: الزجاج
BIQAI-FULL:v5p212/r14.claim: Al-Zajjaj distinguishes kharaj as fayʾ from kharj as a tax or jizya.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p212/r15.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p212/r15.speaker: الأصبهاني
BIQAI-FULL:v5p212/r15.claim: Al-Asbahani transmits Abu Amr ibn al-Ala’s distinction: kharaj is an obligatory payment, whereas kharj is a voluntary gift.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p212/r15.anchor: شئل أبو عمرو بن العلاء فقال : الخراج ما لزمك

BIQAI-FULL:v5p212/r16.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p212/r16.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p212/r16.claim: God’s reward is better than payment from them because it is never cut off or withheld, even from sinners; calling it a due payment hints that God has pledged every servant’s provision without fail.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p212/r16.anchor: لأن خراجه غير مقطوع ولا ممنوع عن أحد من عباده المسيئين

BIQAI-FULL:v5p212/r17.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p212/r17.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p212/r17.claim: God knows what benefits or harms each recipient and provides accordingly, without making anyone ask.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p212/r17.anchor: ما يصلح كل مرزوق وما يفسده

DURR-FULL:v6p109/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p109/r6.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v6p109/r6.claim: Qatada explains the question as asking whether the Prophet seeks payment from them for the message delivered to them.
DURR-FULL:v6p109/r6.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله {بل أتيناهم بذكرهم} قال: هذا القرآن وفي قوله {أم تسألهم أجرا} يقول: أم تسألهم

DURR-FULL:v6p109/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p109/r7.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v6p109/r7.claim: Al-Hasan glosses kharj as a reward or wage.
DURR-FULL:v6p109/r7.anchor: عن الحسن في قوله {خرجا} قال: أجرا

DURR-FULL:v6p109/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p109/r8.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v6p109/r8.claim: Mujahid says the discussion of kharj and the preceding account concerns the Quraysh unbelievers.
DURR-FULL:v6p109/r8.anchor: عن مجاهد قال: الخرج وما قبلها من القصة لكفار قريش

DURR-FULL:v6p109/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p109/r9.speaker: عاصم
DURR-FULL:v6p109/r9.claim: Asim recited the first occurrence without an alif and the second with an alif.
DURR-FULL:v6p109/r9.anchor: عن عاصم أنه قرأ {أم تسألهم خرجا} بغير ألف {فخراج ربك} بالألف

DURR-FULL:v6p109/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p109/r10.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v6p109/r10.claim: Al-Hasan is reported to have recited the two forms as kharjan and fa-kharāju rabbika.
DURR-FULL:v6p109/r10.anchor: عن الحسن أنه قرأ {أم تسألهم خرجا فخراج ربك خير}

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p96/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p96/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p96/r1.claim: أم transitions from the previous question about their supposed madness to a new question about what could motivate their rejection.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p96/r1.anchor: للانتقال إلى استفهام آخر عن دواعي إعراضهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p96/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p96/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p96/r2.claim: The implied question is a denial: they cannot claim that stinginess about payment is why they reject the messenger, since he asks no payment; even if he had, he returned it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p96/r2.anchor: والاستفهام المقدر هنا إنكاري ، أي ما تسألهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p96/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p96/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p96/r3.claim: The hypothetical payment taunt echoes other verses denying that the messenger seeks wages, including two formulations presented sarcastically.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p96/r3.anchor: قل ما سألتكم من أجر فهو لكم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p96/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p96/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p96/r4.claim: This question rules out any cause of rejection originating with the messenger; after earlier questions about their own motives, responsibility lies with them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p96/r4.anchor: فالاستفهام الذي في قوله { أم تسألهم خرجا } إنكاري

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p96/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p96/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p96/r5.claim: خرج is a designated levy or gift imposed on persons or land, such as a tribute.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p96/r5.anchor: والخرج : العطاء المعين على الذوات أو على الأرضين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p96/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p96/r6.speaker: ابن الأعرابي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p96/r6.claim: Ibn al-Aʿrābī distinguishes the terms: kharj is levied on persons, whereas kharāj is levied on land.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p96/r6.anchor: وعن ابن الأعرابي : التفرقة بينهما بأن الخرج الإتاوة على الذوات

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p96/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p96/r7.speaker: قيل
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p96/r7.claim: Another reported distinction makes kharj a voluntary contribution and kharāj a payment owed.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p96/r7.anchor: وقيل الخرج : ما تبرع به المعطي والخراج : ما لزمه أداؤه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p96/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p96/r8.speaker: الزمخشري
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p96/r8.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī’s argument treats kharj as broader than kharāj; the transmitted wording that reverses this is corrected in al-Farāʾid as quoted by al-Tibi.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p96/r8.anchor: ( الكشاف ) : والوجه أن الخرج أخص من الخراج

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p96/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p96/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p96/r9.claim: Kharj is broader than kharāj, as the longer form adds meaning; if the prophet asked people for a little payment, the Creator’s greater gift would still be better, so this distinction is preferable to assuming synonyms.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p96/r9.anchor: وهذا الذي ينبغي التعويل عليه لأن الأصل في اللغة عدم الترادف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p97/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p97/r1.speaker: الجمهور
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p97/r1.claim: The majority read خرجا فخراج ربك خير.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p97/r1.anchor: قرأ الجمهور { أم تسألهم خرجا فخراج ربك خير }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p97/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p97/r2.speaker: ابن عامر
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p97/r2.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir reads خرجا فخرج ربك.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p97/r2.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر { خرجا فخرج ربك }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p97/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p97/r3.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وخلف
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p97/r3.claim: Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī, and Khalaf read خراجا فخراج ربك.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p97/r3.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي وخلف { أم تسألهم خراجا فخراج ربك خير }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p97/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p97/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p97/r4.claim: If the words are synonyms, the majority reading varies the wording to avoid an awkward nearby repetition; this is especially apt compared with the three-word gap before أجري is repeated elsewhere.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p97/r4.anchor: فتوجيهها على اعتبار ترادف الكلمتين أنها جرت على التفنن في الكلام تجنبا لإعادة اللفظ

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p97/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p97/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p97/r5.claim: If the words differ in scope as al-Zamakhsharī argues, the majority reading combines verbal variation with an intensifying rhetorical effect.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p97/r5.anchor: وأما على اعتبار الفرق الذي اختاره الزمخشري فتوجيهها باشتمالها على التفنن وعلى محسن المبالغة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p97/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p97/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p97/r6.claim: The readings that repeat the same form suit synonymy through paired verbal symmetry; they do not fit al-Zamakhsharī’s distinction between the terms.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p97/r6.anchor: فتوجيهها على طريقة الترادف أنهما وردتا على اختيار المتكلم في الاستعمال مع محسن المزاوجة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p97/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p97/r7.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p97/r7.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says the verses exhaust their excuses: the messenger is known and unlikely to invent his claim, seeks no worldly wealth, calls to Islam, exposes their failure to reflect and blind inherited religion, and faces baseless charges of madness despite clear signs.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p97/r7.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) : ألزمهم الله الحجة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p97/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p97/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p97/r8.claim: The parenthetical praise of God as the best provider completes the point by affirming His abundant favor and reinforcing that His provision is better.

BURSEVI:v6p68/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p68/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p68/r5.claim: The question turns from the rebuke over their claim that the Messenger was possessed to another rebuke: do they allege that he asks payment for his mission?
BURSEVI:v6p68/r5.anchor: انتقال من توبيخهم بما ذكر من قولهم أو يقولون به جنة

BURSEVI:v6p68#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p68#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p68#2/r1.claim: Kharj means a payment or wage; the implication is that they refuse to believe because they imagine he seeks one.
BURSEVI:v6p68#2/r1.anchor: أي : جعلا وأجر فلأجل ذلك لا يؤمنون بك

BURSEVI:v6p68#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p68#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p68#2/r2.claim: God’s provision in this life and reward in the next are broader and more lasting than their payment, leaving the Messenger independent of their gifts.
BURSEVI:v6p68#2/r2.anchor: فإن رزق ربك في الدنيا وثوابه في العقبى خير لك من ذلك لسعته ودوامه ففيه استغناء لك عن عطائهم

BURSEVI:v6p68#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p68#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p68#2/r3.claim: Kharj commonly means what one pays out to another; kharaj commonly denotes land tax, suggesting abundance and regularity, so it is the stronger term for God’s gift.
BURSEVI:v6p68#2/r3.anchor: والخرج بإزاء الدخل يقال لكل ما تخرجه إلى غيرك والخراج غالب في الضريبة على الأرض ففيه إشعار بالكثرة واللزوم

BURSEVI:v6p68#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p68#2/r4.speaker: تفسير المناسبات
BURSEVI:v6p68#2/r4.claim: The commentary says God calls it kharaj to signal that He has pledged each person’s provision to Himself with a promise He will not break.
BURSEVI:v6p68#2/r4.anchor: تفسير المناسبات" : وكأنه سماه خراجا إشارة إلى أنه أوجب رزق كل أحد

BURSEVI:v6p68#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p68#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p68#2/r5.claim: God is the best giver of recompense for work because His gift neither ends nor becomes clouded; this explains the superiority of His provision.
BURSEVI:v6p68#2/r5.anchor: أي خير من أعطى عوضا على عمل لأن ما يعطيه لا ينقطع ولا يتكدر وهو تقدير لخيرية خراجه تعالى

BURSEVI:v6p68#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p68#2/r6.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v6p68#2/r6.claim: The firmly grounded knowers of God do not stain their luminous hearts with worldly or otherworldly desires while calling people to God through God.
BURSEVI:v6p68#2/r6.anchor: التأويلات النجمية" : فيه إشارة إلى أن العلماء بالله الراسخين في العلم

BURSEVI:v6p68#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p68#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p68#2/r7.claim: The Persian couplet warns that an exegete loses by selling knowledge and skill for bread, reinforcing the call to avoid payment-seeking.
BURSEVI:v6p68#2/r7.anchor: زيان ميكند مرد تفسير دان كه علم وهنر ميفر وشدبنان

BURSEVI:v6p68#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p68#2/r8.speaker: الشيخ الأكبر
BURSEVI:v6p68#2/r8.claim: Ibn al-ʿArabi’s position permits a preacher to take wages, among the most lawful earnings, though abstaining is better; prophets chose their reward from God rather than people.
BURSEVI:v6p68#2/r8.anchor: قال حضرة الشيخ الأكبر قدس سره الأطهر في "الفتوحات المكية" : مذهبنا أن للواعظ أخذ الأجرة

BURSEVI:v6p68#3/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p68#3/r8.speaker: بهلول
BURSEVI:v6p68#3/r8.claim: Bahlul refuses Harun’s offer to repay his debts or provide a pension: debt cannot be paid with debt, and God will not remember Harun while forgetting His other servant.
BURSEVI:v6p68#3/r8.anchor: الدين لا يقضى بدين أد أموال الناس إليهم

BURSEVI:v6p68#3/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p68#3/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p68#3/r9.claim: Bahlul’s final answer points to this verse: provision arriving unexpectedly from God is better than provision from a specified source.
BURSEVI:v6p68#3/r9.anchor: وأشار بهلول في قوله الأخير إلى مضمون قوله تعالى : {فخراج ربك خير}

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p151#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p151#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p151#2/r1.claim: This reproaches them as if asking whether the Prophet demanded payment and they resented or found the burden heavy.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p151#2/r1.anchor: هذا توبيخ لهم كأنه قال: أم سألتهم مالا فقلقوا بذلك واستثقلوا من أجله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p151#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p151#2/r3.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وعاصم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p151#2/r3.claim: Ibn Kathīr, Nāfiʿ, Abū ʿAmr, and ʿĀṣim read “kharjan fa-kharāj.”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p151#2/r3.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وعاصم «خرجا فخراج»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p151#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p151#2/r5.speaker: الأصمعي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p151#2/r5.claim: Al-Aṣmaʿī distinguishes “kharj,” a one-time payment, from recurring “kharāj” paid at intervals; Ibn ʿAṭiyya says this is usage, since the words mean the same linguistically.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p151#2/r5.anchor: قال الأصمعي: الخرج الجعل مرة واحدة والخراج ما تردد لأوقات ما

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p151#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p151#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p151#2/r6.claim: “Your Lord's kharāj” may mean His reward, named as compensation in this context.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p151#2/r6.anchor: وقوله فخراج ربك يريد ثوابه سماه «خراجا» من حيث كان معادلا للخراج

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p151#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p151#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p151#2/r7.claim: Alternatively, it may mean your Lord's provision, supported by the following description of Him as the best provider.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p151#2/r7.anchor: ويحتمل أن يريد فخراج ربك رزق ربك ويؤيد هذا قوله وهو خير الرازقين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p484#6/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p484#6/r1.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وعاصم وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p484#6/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir, Nafiʿ, Abu ʿAmr, and ʿAsim read kharjan without alif then kharāj with it; Ibn ʿAmir reads both without alif, while Hamza and al-Kisaʾi read both with alif.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p484#6/r1.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير ونافع وابو عمرو وعاصم خرجا بغير الف فخراج بألف وقرأ ابن عامر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p484#6/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p484#6/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p484#6/r2.claim: Kharj means payment or property; God's reward and recompense are better, and He is the best giver.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p484#6/r2.anchor: ومعنى خرجا أجرا ومالا فخراج ربك أي فما يعطيك ربك من أجره وثوابه خير

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p484#6/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p484#6/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p484#6/r3.claim: The question alerts them that the Prophet is not asking them for payment; it does not imply that he asked.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p484#6/r3.anchor: وهذا على سبيل التنبيه لهم أنه لم يسالهم أجرا لا أنه قد سألهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p485/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p485/r1.speaker: الحسن
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p485/r1.claim: Al-Ḥasan explains kharj as a wage.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p485/r1.anchor: وقوله: {أم تسألهم خرجا} : قال الحسن: أجرا.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p485/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p485/r2.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p485/r2.claim: Qatāda explains kharj as a payment or grant.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p485/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p485/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p485/r3.claim: The Prophet asks no wage or payment for calling people to guidance; he seeks God's abundant reward, as other verses also say.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p485/r3.anchor: أنت لا تسألهم أجرة ولا جعلا ولا شيئا على دعوتك إياهم إلى الهدى

JISHUMI:v7p5073/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5073/r1.speaker: أبو جعفر ونافع وابن كثير وعاصم وأبو عمرو ويعقوب
JISHUMI:v7p5073/r1.claim: These readers read خرج without alif and خراج with alif.
JISHUMI:v7p5073/r1.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر ونافع وابن كثير وعاصم وأبو عمرو ويعقوب: خرجا بغير ألف

JISHUMI:v7p5073/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5073/r2.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
JISHUMI:v7p5073/r2.claim: Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī use alif in both words.

JISHUMI:v7p5073/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5073/r3.speaker: ابن عامر
JISHUMI:v7p5073/r3.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir reads both forms without alif.
JISHUMI:v7p5073/r3.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر بغير ألف فيهما

JISHUMI:v7p5073/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5073/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5073/r4.claim: Some say خرج and خراج have the same sense, whose basic meaning is revenue or levy.
JISHUMI:v7p5073/r4.anchor: قيل: هما واحد، وأصلهما الغلة والإتاوة

JISHUMI:v7p5073/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5073/r5.speaker: النضر بن شميل
JISHUMI:v7p5073/r5.claim: Al-Naḍr ibn Shumayl reports Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ’s distinction: خراج is obligatory, while خرج is voluntary.
JISHUMI:v7p5073/r5.anchor: وعن النضر بن شميل: سألت أبا عمرو بن العلاء

JISHUMI:v7p5073/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5073/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5073/r6.claim: Both words originally refer to something collected by assessment; they are verbal nouns and do not form plurals.
JISHUMI:v7p5073/r6.anchor: وأصله ما يخرج على سبيل التوظيف، ومنه: خراج الرأس والأرض

JISHUMI:v7p5076/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5076/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5076/r5.claim: Since God’s provision is best, what is unlawful does not count as provision from God.
JISHUMI:v7p5076/r5.anchor: وتدل على أن رزقه خير، فيوجب أن الحرام ليس برزق

JISHUMI:v7p5076/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5076/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5076/r6.claim: The wording خير الرازقين implies that there are other providers among created beings.
JISHUMI:v7p5076/r6.anchor: وتدل على أن في العباد من يرزق، ولذلك قال (وهو خير الرازقين)

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p198#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p198#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p198#2/r1.claim: Readings include kharājan fa-kharāj, kharjan fa-kharj, and kharjan fa-kharāj.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p198#2/r1.anchor: قرىء : ( خراجا فخراج ) و ( خرجا فخرج ) ( خرجا فخراج )

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p198#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p198#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p198#2/r2.claim: Kharj or kharāj can denote land dues paid to the ruler or a worker’s wages or stipend.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p198#2/r2.anchor: وهو ما تخرجه إلى الإمام من زكاة أرضك . وإلى كل عامل من أجرته

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p198#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p198#2/r3.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p198#2/r3.claim: One distinction is that kharj is voluntary giving, while kharāj is an obligatory payment.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p198#2/r3.anchor: وقيل : الخرج : ما تبرعت به . والخراج : ما لزمك أداؤه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p198#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p198#2/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p198#2/r4.claim: He prefers kharj as narrower and kharāj as broader, since added wording adds meaning; this favors kharjan fa-kharāj.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p198#2/r4.anchor: والوجه أن الخرج أخص من الخراج ، كقولك : خراج القرية ، وخرج الكردة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p198#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p198#2/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p198#2/r5.claim: The question means: do you ask them for a small human payment for guiding them, when the greater gift from the Creator is better?
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p198#2/r5.anchor: يعني : أم تسألهم على هدايتك لهم قليلا من عطاء الخلق ، فالكثير من عطاء الخالق خير

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p61/r18.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p61/r18.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p61/r18.claim: Al-Mawardi glosses kharjan here as an affair or demand.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p61/r18.anchor: قوله : { أم تسألهم خرجا } يعني أمرا .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p61/r19.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p61/r19.speaker: الكلبي
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p61/r19.claim: Al-Kalbi interprets the Lord's kharaj as sustenance in this world, better than what they could give.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p61/r19.anchor: أحدهما : فرزق ربك في الدنيا خير منهم , قاله الكلبي .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p61/r20.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p61/r20.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p61/r20.claim: Al-Hasan interprets the Lord's kharaj as the reward of the Hereafter, better than theirs.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p61/r20.anchor: الثاني : فأجر ربك في الآخرة خير منه , قاله الحسن .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p61/r21.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p61/r21.speaker: أبو عمرو بن العلاء
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p61/r21.claim: Abu ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAla distinguishes kharj from people from kharaj from land.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p61/r21.anchor: وذكر أبو عمرو بن العلاء الفرق بين الخرج والخراج فقال : الخرج من الرقاب : والخراج من الأرض .

MUQATIL:23:72-73/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:23:72-73/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:23:72-73/r1.claim: The requested kharj is payment for believing in the Qur'an.
MUQATIL:23:72-73/r1.anchor: أم تسألهم } يا محمد { خرجا } أجرا على الإيمان بالقرآن

MUQATIL:23:72-73/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:23:72-73/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:23:72-73/r2.claim: God's reward is better than the payment they might give.
MUQATIL:23:72-73/r2.anchor: فخراج ربك } يعني فأجر ربك { خير } يعني أفضل من خراجهم

NASAFI-FULL:v3p127/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p127/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p127/r1.claim: Hijazi, Basri, and Asim read kharjan followed by kharāju; Ali and Hamza read kharjan followed by kharju; the Shami reading has kharājan followed by kharāju.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p127/r1.anchor: ﴿ أم تسألهم خرجا فخراج ربك خير ﴾ حجازى وبصرى وعاصم خرجا فخرج على وحمزة شامى خراجا فخراج

NASAFI-FULL:v3p127/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p127/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p127/r2.claim: Kharaj is what one pays a ruler as land tax or a worker as wages; kharj is narrower, while kharaj is broader, as in village revenue versus Kufa’s levy.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p127/r2.anchor: وهو ما تخرجه إلى الإمام من زكاة أرضك وإلى كل عامل من أجرته وجعله والخرج أخص من الخراج

NASAFI-FULL:v3p127/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p127/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p127/r3.claim: The first reading is preferable because the greater length of kharaj suits its broader meaning.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p127/r3.anchor: فزيادة اللفظ لزيادة المعنى ولذا حسنت القراءة الأولى

NASAFI-FULL:v3p127/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p127/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p127/r4.claim: The question asks whether the Prophet seeks even a small payment from people for guiding them, when the Creator’s ample provision is better.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p127/r4.anchor: يعنى أم تسألهم على هدايتك لهم قليلا من عطاء الخلق فالكثير من الخالق خير

NASAFI-FULL:v3p127/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p127/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p127/r5.claim: God is the best of givers.

QURTUBI-FULL:23:72/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:72/r1.speaker: الحسن وغيره
QURTUBI-FULL:23:72/r1.claim: Al-Hasan and others take the question to mean: do you ask them for payment for what you have brought them?
QURTUBI-FULL:23:72/r1.anchor: أي أجرا على ما جئتهم به قاله الحسن وغيره

QURTUBI-FULL:23:72/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:72/r2.speaker: حمزة والكسائي والأعمش ويحيى بن وثاب وابن عامر وأبو حيوة
QURTUBI-FULL:23:72/r2.claim: Hamza, al-Kisaʾi, al-Aʿmash, and Yahya b. Waththab read the first word with an alif; the others without. All read the second with an alif except Ibn ʿAmir and Abu Haywa, who omit it.
QURTUBI-FULL:23:72/r2.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي والأعمش ويحيى بن وثاب «خراجا» بألف. الباقون بغير ألف

QURTUBI-FULL:23:72/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:72/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:23:72/r3.claim: The sense is: are you asking them for provision? Your Lord’s provision is better.
QURTUBI-FULL:23:72/r3.anchor: والمعنى: أم تسألهم رزقا فرزق ربك خير

QURTUBI-FULL:23:72/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:72/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:23:72/r4.claim: No one can provide sustenance or bestow favor as God does.
QURTUBI-FULL:23:72/r4.anchor: أي ليس يقدر أحد أن يرزق مثل رزقه، ولا ينعم مثل إنعامه

QURTUBI-FULL:23:72/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:72/r5.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:23:72/r5.claim: Al-Hasan also says God’s reward for obedience and calling people to Him is better than worldly gain; Quraysh offered to make the Prophet their richest man, but he did not accept.
QURTUBI-FULL:23:72/r5.anchor: وقد عرضوا عليك أموالهم حتى تكون كأعين رجل من قريش فلم تجبهم إلى ذلك قال معناه الحسن

QURTUBI-FULL:23:72/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:72/r6.speaker: الأخفش
QURTUBI-FULL:23:72/r6.claim: Al-Akhfash says kharj and kharaj have the same meaning, though varying the wording is more elegant.
QURTUBI-FULL:23:72/r6.anchor: والخرج والخراج واحد، إلا أن اختلاف الكلام أحسن قاله الأخفش

QURTUBI-FULL:23:72/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:72/r7.speaker: أبو حاتم
QURTUBI-FULL:23:72/r7.claim: Abu Hatim distinguishes kharj as a payment or fee and kharaj as a grant.
QURTUBI-FULL:23:72/r7.anchor: وقال أبو حاتم: الخرج الجعل، والخراج العطاء

QURTUBI-FULL:23:72/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:72/r8.speaker: المبرد
QURTUBI-FULL:23:72/r8.claim: Al-Mubarrad says kharj is the verbal noun, while kharaj is the noun.

QURTUBI-FULL:23:72/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:72/r9.speaker: أبو عمرو بن العلاء
QURTUBI-FULL:23:72/r9.claim: Abu ʿAmr b. al-ʿAlaʾ distinguishes kharaj as what is owed from kharj as what one gives voluntarily.
QURTUBI-FULL:23:72/r9.anchor: فقال: الخراج ما لزمك، والخرج ما تبرعت به

QURTUBI-FULL:23:72/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:72/r10.speaker: أبو عمرو بن العلاء
QURTUBI-FULL:23:72/r10.claim: Another distinction attributed to Abu ʿAmr is that kharj is income from persons and kharaj income from land; al-Thaʿlabi and al-Mawardi transmit the two distinctions respectively.
QURTUBI-FULL:23:72/r10.anchor: وعنه أن الخرج من الرقاب، والخراج من الأرض. ذكر الأول الثعلبي والثاني الماوردي

RAZI-FULL:v23p98/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p98/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p98/r5.claim: The two occurrences have readings kharjan and kharājan.
RAZI-FULL:v23p98/r5.anchor: أم تسألهم خرجا فخراج ربك خير } وقرىء خراجا

RAZI-FULL:v23p98/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p98/r6.speaker: أبو عمرو بن العلاء
RAZI-FULL:v23p98/r6.claim: Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ defines kharj as a voluntary gift and kharāj as an obligatory payment.
RAZI-FULL:v23p98/r6.anchor: قال أبو عمرو بن العلاء الخرج ما تبرعت به والخراج ما لزمك أداؤه

RAZI-FULL:v23p98/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p98/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p98/r7.claim: Kharj is narrower than kharāj; the longer form suits the greater meaning.
RAZI-FULL:v23p98/r7.anchor: الخرج أخص من الخراج كقولك خراج القرية وخرج الكردة

RAZI-FULL:v23p98/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p98/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p98/r8.claim: The Prophet asks no small payment for guiding people; God’s greater gift is better than anything people give.
RAZI-FULL:v23p98/r8.anchor: يعني أم تسألهم على هدايتهم قليلا من عطاء الخلق

RAZI-FULL:v23p98/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p98/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p98/r9.claim: This refutes the suspicion that the Prophet seeks payment and shows the rejecters are without excuse.
RAZI-FULL:v23p98/r9.anchor: على أن هذه التهمة بعيدة عنه

RAZI-FULL:v23p98/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p98/r10.speaker: الجبائي
RAZI-FULL:v23p98/r10.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī argues no servant equals God’s provision; the phrase also implies servants provide for one another, or “best providers” would make no sense.
RAZI-FULL:v23p98/r10.anchor: قال الجبائي دل قوله تعالى : { وهو خير الرزقين }

STUDYQURAN:23:72/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:23:72/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:23:72/r1.claim: The Quran often emphasizes that messengers ask for no recompense, as in the listed verses.
STUDYQURAN:23:72/r1.anchor: The theme of messengers asking no recompense appears often in the Quran

TAB-FULL:v17p90#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p90#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v17p90#2/r1.claim: The rhetorical question means Muhammad asks no payment for the counsel and truth he brought; God's reward for obeying Him and seeking His pleasure is better. They recoiled proudly, and 42:23 is cited as his commanded response.
TAB-FULL:v17p90#2/r1.anchor: وابتغاء مرضاته خير لك من ذلك

TAB-FULL:v17p90#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p90#2/r2.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v17p90#2/r2.claim: Al-Ḥasan glosses kharj as payment or a reward.
TAB-FULL:v17p90#2/r2.anchor: عن الحسن: {أم تسألهم خرجا فخراج ربك خير} [المؤمنون: 72] قال: «أجرا»

TAB-FULL:v17p90#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p90#2/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v17p90#2/r3.claim: Kharāj and kharj are both verbal nouns and have no plural form.
TAB-FULL:v17p90#2/r3.anchor: وأصل الخراج والخرج: مصدران لا يجمعان

TABATABAI:23:72/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:23:72/r2.speaker: مجمع البيان
TABATABAI:23:72/r2.claim: Majmaʿ al-Bayān says kharāj and kharj share the sense of revenue or produce paid as an assigned due.
TABATABAI:23:72/r2.anchor: قال في مجمع البيان أصل الخراج والخرج واحد وهو الغلة التي يخرج على سبيل الوظيفة

TABATABAI:23:72/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:23:72/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:23:72/r3.claim: This is the fourth rejected excuse: they allege the Prophet asks them for a customary payment, but God provides for him, so he needs no revenue from them; compare 11:51.
TABATABAI:23:72/r3.anchor: أي مالا يدفعونه إليك على سبيل الرسم والوظيفة

TABATABAI:23:72/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:23:72/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:23:72/r4.claim: The first two rejected excuses concern the Qur’an and the religion’s novelty relative to earlier peoples, respectively.
TABATABAI:23:72/r4.anchor: فأولها { أفلم يدبروا القول } راجع إلى القرآن والثاني

TABATABAI:23:72/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:23:72/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:23:72/r5.claim: The third excuse targets the Prophet himself with the claim of madness; the fourth targets his conduct by alleging that he asks for payment.
TABATABAI:23:72/r5.anchor: والثالث { أم يقولون به جنة } إلى نفس النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم، والرابع { أم تسألهم خرجا } إلى سيرته

TABRISI:23:72-77/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:23:72-77/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:23:72-77/r1.claim: Kharj and khiraj mean assessed revenue, including land tax; both are verbal nouns, and readings were discussed at 18:94.
TABRISI:23:72-77/r1.anchor: أصل الخراج والخرج واحد وهو الغلة التي تخرج على سبيل الوظيفة

TABRISI:23:72-77/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:23:72-77/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:23:72-77/r8.claim: The question denies Muhammad asks payment for Quran and faith; money could make him seem suspect or burden acceptance.
TABRISI:23:72-77/r8.anchor: أي أجرا ومالا يعطونك فيورث ذلك تهمة في حالك أو يثقل عليهم قبول قولك

TABRISI:23:72-77/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:23:72-77/r9.speaker: الكلبي
TABRISI:23:72-77/r9.claim: Al-Kalbi takes the Lord’s khiraj as worldly provision, better than payment from the people.
TABRISI:23:72-77/r9.anchor: فخراج ربك خير } أي فرزق ربك في الدنيا خير منه عن الكلبي

TABRISI:23:72-77/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:23:72-77/r10.speaker: الحسن
TABRISI:23:72-77/r10.claim: Al-Hasan takes the Lord’s khiraj as the hereafter reward, better than their payment.
TABRISI:23:72-77/r10.anchor: وقيل: فأجر ربك في الآخرة خير منه عن الحسن

TABRISI:23:72-77/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:23:72-77/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:23:72-77/r11.claim: God is the best giver and rewarder; servants may provide for others by His permission.
TABRISI:23:72-77/r11.anchor: أي أفضل من أعطى وآجر وفي هذا دلالة على أن في العباد من يرزق غيره بإذن الله

FARRA:v2p239/r2.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p239/r2.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p239/r2.claim: خرج means payment or reward for what the Messenger brought; his Lord’s reward is better.
FARRA:v2p239/r2.anchor: يقول: على ما جئت به، يريد: أجرا، فأجر ربك خير.

THALABI:v7p52/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p52/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p52/r5.claim: Kharj means payment, wage, or gift; kharj and kharāj can also denote revenue, tax, or tribute, such as dues on a slave or land.
THALABI:v7p52/r5.anchor: أم تسألهم على ما جئتهم به خرجا أجرا وجعلا وأصل الخرج والخراج الغلة والضريبة والأتاوة

THALABI:v7p52/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p52/r6.speaker: النضر بن شميل
THALABI:v7p52/r6.claim: Al-Nadr ibn Shumayl quotes Abu Amr ibn al-Ala distinguishing kharāj as an obligatory due from kharj as a voluntary payment.
THALABI:v7p52/r6.anchor: وقال النضر بن شميل: سألت أبا عمرو بن العلاء عن الفرق بين الخرج والخراج فقال: الخراج ما لزمك ووجب عليك أداؤه

THALABI:v7p52/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p52/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p52/r7.claim: God’s provision and reward are better than any payment from the people, and He is the best provider.
THALABI:v7p52/r7.anchor: قال الله سبحانه: فخراج ربك رزقه وثوابه خير وهو خير الرازقين

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p299#3/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p299#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p299#3/r1.claim: Kharj means a payment or levy, which the people would find burdensome.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p299#3/r1.anchor: أم تسألهم خرجا} أي خراجا، فهم يستثقلون ذلك.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p299#3/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p299#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p299#3/r2.claim: Kharāj from God means His provision.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p36/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p36/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p36/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses خرجًا as money they would give Muhammad.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p36/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد مالا يعطونك

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p36/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p36/r2.speaker: مقاتل، أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p36/r2.claim: Muqātil and Abū Isḥāq say Muhammad did not ask payment for their belief in the Qur'an or for what he brought them.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p36/r2.anchor: وقال أبو إسحاق: أي لم تسألهم على ما أتيتهم به أجرا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p36/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p36/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p36/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains God's kharāj as His gift.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p36/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس: فعطاء ربك خير

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p36/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p36/r4.speaker: مقاتل، author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p36/r4.claim: Muqātil says God's reward is better than their payment; the author says God's reward and recompense are better for Muhammad.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p36/r4.anchor: وقال مقاتل: فأجر ربك أفضل من خراجهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p36/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p36/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p36/r5.claim: God is best in giving, giving abundantly, and rewarding.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p36/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p36/r6.speaker: أهل المعاني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p36/r6.claim: The verse indicates that others besides God provide, since otherwise calling God the best provider would not be apt.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p36/r6.anchor: قال أهل المعاني: قد دلت الآية على أن غير الله يرزق

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p36/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p36/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p36/r7.claim: Arabic usage can say a ruler provided for his soldiers and they received provision.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p36/r7.anchor: ويقال: رزق الأمير جنده فارتزقوا ارتزاقا

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:23:71-72/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:23:71-72/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:23:71-72/r4.claim: Muhammad is asked whether he seeks a fee or payment from them; God's gift and reward are better.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:23:71-72/r4.anchor: جعلا وأجرا { فخراج ربك } فعطاء ربك وثوابه

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p411/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p411/r1.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p411/r1.claim: Qatadah says the question means: do you ask them a payment for what you brought? The implied answer is no.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p411/r1.anchor: قال قتادة: أم تسألهم على ما أتيتهم به جعلا، أي إنك لا تسألهم عليه أجرا

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p411/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p411/r2.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p411/r2.claim: The reward from God in the Hereafter is better than any worldly wage they might pay.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p411/r2.anchor: أجر ربك أي ثوابه في الآخرة خير من أجرهم لو أعطوك في الدنيا أجرا

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p411/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p411/r3.speaker: السدي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p411/r3.claim: God is the best provider: He may provide people through one another, allotting one person's provision through another's hands.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p411/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p411/r4.speaker: أم الدرداء
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p411/r4.claim: Umm al-Darda says God does not send coins from heaven but provides through people; accept provision that comes, use it if needed, otherwise pass it to needy brethren, and do not reject God's provision.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p411/r4.anchor: عن أم الدرداء قالت: ما بال أحدكم يقول: اللهم ارزقني، وقد علم أن الله لا يمطر عليه من السماء دنانير ولا دراهم

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p411/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p411/r5.speaker: النبي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p411/r5.claim: The Prophet told Umar to accept a gift he had neither sought nor pursued, then spend it if needed or give it to those in need.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p411/r5.anchor: عن عمران القصير قال: لقيت مكحولا بمكة، فأعطاني شيئا فانقبضت عنه فقال: خذه

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p411/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p411/r6.speaker: قبيصة بن ذؤيب
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p411/r6.claim: Qubaysa reports that Umar gave Qurayshi Abdullah ibn Sa'd a thousand dinars and urged him to accept an unsolicited gift, as the Prophet had instructed Umar.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p411/r6.anchor: عن قبيصة بن ذؤيب أن عمر بن الخطاب دفع إلى عبد الله بن سعد، رجل من قريش، ألف دينار

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:72/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:72/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:72/r1.claim: The fee question does not imply that the Prophet asked payment for his mission; it asks rhetorically whether they turn away because he charges them.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:72/r1.anchor: Hz. Peygamber’in peygamberlik görevi için bir karşılık talep etmiş olabileceği hatıra gelmemelidir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:72/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:72/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:72/r2.claim: God will reward the Prophet better for his mission; his sole aim is to call people to the straight path, Islam.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:72/r2.anchor: görevini yapmanın karşılığı olarak Allah seni daha iyisi ile ödüllendirecektir. Senin tek amacın, onları “dosdoğru bir yol”a yani İslâm’a çağırmaktır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:72/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:72/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:72/r3.claim: The Meccan idolaters strayed from the path to right belief and conduct despite the Prophet’s efforts.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:72/r3.anchor: Resûlullah’ın bütün çabalarına rağmen Mekke putperestleri doğru inanca ve yaşayışa götüren yoldan sapıyorlardı

NAHHAS:v3p119/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p119/r1.speaker: الأخفش
NAHHAS:v3p119/r1.claim: Al-Akhfash says kharj is singular, though using different wording in the paired terms is better.
NAHHAS:v3p119/r1.anchor: قال الأخفش الخرج واحد إلا أن اختلاف الكلام أحسن

NAHHAS:v3p119/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p119/r2.speaker: أبو حاتم
NAHHAS:v3p119/r2.claim: Abū Ḥātim distinguishes kharj as a payment from kharāj as a gift or allowance.
NAHHAS:v3p119/r2.anchor: وقال أبو حاتم الخرج الجعل والخراج العطاء وقول محمد بن يزيد

NAHHAS:v3p119/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p119/r3.speaker: محمد بن يزيد
NAHHAS:v3p119/r3.claim: Muḥammad ibn Yazīd analyzes kharj as a verbal noun and kharāj as a substantive noun.
NAHHAS:v3p119/r3.anchor: وقول محمد بن يزيد الخرج المصدر والخراج الاسم والمعنى أم تسألهم

NAHHAS:v3p119/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p119/r4.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p119/r4.claim: The question means, “Are you asking them for provision?” God’s provision is better, and none provides or bestows favor like Him.
NAHHAS:v3p119/r4.anchor: والمعنى أم تسألهم رزقا فرزق ربك خير وهو خير الرازقين أي ليس أحد يرزق مثل رزقه ولا ينعم مثل إنعامه

DAMGHANI:v1p152/r8.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p152/r8.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p152/r8.claim: خرج in the question about asking for payment means reward; God's reward is better.
DAMGHANI:v1p152/r8.anchor: فوجه منهما : الخراج بمعنى الثواب قوله تعالى في سورة المؤمنين
